strengths: Addresses practical and important problem of cross-domain deployment for E2E autonomous driving
Comprehensive experimental evaluation including cross-city generalization, active learning, robustness to degradations, and long-tail scenarios
Strong empirical results: 16% L2 error reduction, 54% collision rate reduction with GP trajectory prediction on VAD-T
Flexible framework compatible with different base E2E models (VAD, SparseDrive) without requiring LLMs
Effective uncertainty-guided active learning via GP predictive variance
Good visualization (Figure 2) demonstrating improved representation separability with RoCA
Detailed training procedure, pseudocode (Algorithm 1), and computational cost analysis provided for reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited dataset diversity: evaluation only on nuScenes with two cities (Boston, Singapore); no validation on Waymo, KITTI, or other datasets weakens cross-domain robustness claims
Codebook construction methodology critically underspecified: clustering algorithm, hyperparameters, and sensitivity analysis all missing, yet this is a core component affecting performance
Significant computational overhead (27-36% latency increase) for real-time autonomous driving applications not thoroughly analyzed or justified

Weak theoretical justification for GP choice: why GPs are suitable for cross-domain robustness insufficiently motivated; connection between token reconstruction and trajectory prediction not rigorously established

Crucial design choices lack justification: codebook structure (Nego=48, Nagent=64, C=64) appears arbitrary; gradient freezing during basis token learning unexplained; loss term weighting strategy missing
Uncertainty calibration not addressed: no calibration error metrics, reliability diagrams, or validation that GP uncertainties are trustworthy for safety-critical applications
Claims not fully supported: 'online adaptation' mentioned in abstract but never evaluated; 'long-tail robustness' demonstrated on only three scenario types
Limited baseline comparisons: VLP comparison in appendix only, no comparison with other domain adaptation methods (adversarial adaptation, self-training, feature normalization)
Collision rate metric possibly insensitive: rates of 0.09-0.2% extremely low; missing metrics like success rate, comfort, or trajectory smoothness
No failure case analysis: which domain shifts are handled well versus problematic; when does the basis codebook become insufficient not discussed

strengths: Comprehensive experimental evaluation across closed-loop, open-loop, cross-city, image degradation, and long-tail scenarios with consistent improvements across multiple base models
Strong empirical results: 11.7% ability improvement on Bench2Drive, significant sim-to-real gains, and superior performance on long-tail events and adverse conditions
Practical plug-and-play design that works with different E2E models; no additional inference cost in source-domain training mode; supports multiple adaptation paradigms
Interpretable approach with good token space visualization showing improved clustering and well-calibrated uncertainty estimates demonstrating superiority over MC Dropout and Deep Ensembles
Good reproducibility with detailed algorithms, training procedures, hyperparameters, and timing information provided
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: individual components (GPs, token codebooks, basis learning) are well-established; applying standard GP to E2E driving is relatively incremental

Weak theoretical justification: lacks principled explanation for why joint modeling of p(e,a,trajectories) improves cross-domain generalization; connection between uncertainty and domain robustness is purely empirical

Potential circular dependency issue: base model trained to match GP predictions (Eq. 7) while GP is trained on base model tokens; training convergence and error accumulation in unsupervised adaptation not adequately addressed

Computational overhead dismissed too quickly: Table 10 shows 25-27% latency increase during inference; 37+ hours total training time is substantial; claimed 'no extra inference computation' is misleading for training regularization mode

Codebook construction under-specified: trajectory sampling and clustering procedures vague; no sensitivity analysis on codebook quality/diversity; fixed hyperparameters (Ncode=112, C=64) not justified across domains

Experimental rigor gaps: no error bars/significance tests despite multiple experiments; modest improvements in some cases (<1-2% on collision rate); limited failure case discussion; comparison with VLP only in appendix using different protocol

Incomplete technical details: positive/negative class selection for triplet loss not specified; trajectory space validity constraints not discussed; design choices lack motivation (e.g., why RBF kernel specifically)
